content: A Russian SU-27 fighter jet made an aggressive approach towards a US RC-135U intelligence-gathering plane in international airspace over the Sea of Okhotsk on April 23, amid rising tensions between the US and Russia over Ukraine.
Prince Charles and Camilla will embark on a 12-day tour of Australia and New Zealand, visiting 12 towns and cities, including meeting the new Australian PM Malcolm Turnbull, starting on November 4.
A man has been detained and is being questioned in connection with a September 20 attack on a woman in Sneem, County Kerry.

A former GP, Hugh McGoldrick, who falsified drug trials on patients with sleep disorders, has had his name erased from the medical register after failing to appeal the decision within the given 28-day deadline.
A man's body was found in a wooded area near Dorking, and Surrey Police has arrested a 21-year-old male on suspicion of murder, awaiting the results of a post-mortem examination.

A 21-year-old man, Josh Hanson, was stabbed to death at a bar in Eastcote, London, early Sunday, and Scotland Yard is urging around 40 people who were present at the time to come forward with information.

Hovertravel, a ferry operator, is considering adding a cross-Solent service between Sandown and Southsea, with a provisional plan to operate four 25-minute crossings on Tuesdays and Thursdays in July and August, to boost tourism on the Isle of Wight.
A 30-year-old man was arrested in connection with an attack on a victim by up to eight men in the Heights area, but has since been released on police bail pending further enquiries.
The death toll from floods in India has doubled to over 100 as waters recede, with officials estimating that 450,000 people have been affected in the state.
Arsenal will host Leicester City on Friday, August 11, at 19:45 BST, as part of the Premier League's 25th anniversary season, with Sky Sports having secured rights to screen 10 Friday night matches.

Oldham Athletic Football Club has dismissed Cristian Montano, a 22-year-old player who was arrested as part of a spot-fixing investigation, after a thorough investigation and a swift decision by the board.

A 20-year-old man, Rick Edwards, was given a suspended 12-month jail term and a supervision order after admitting to starting a fire at the former Pontins resort in Brixham in 2014, claiming he did it "for fun".
Wilson, a 30-year-old footballer, rejoined Nottingham Forest from Celtic in 2013 but has been without a team since his release in May.
Australia's slow left-armer Amila Aponso took 4-18 in 9.2 overs as they bowled Sri Lanka out for 206 to win the match by 82 runs, levelling the five-match series at 1-1.
Sale Sharks forward Vadim Cobilas has signed with French Top 14 team Bordeaux, marking his move out of Sale after being out of contract this summer.

India's promising 277-1 against Australia collapsed to 323 all out, with Kane Richardson taking 5-68, after a 212-run partnership between Virat Kohli and Shikhar Dhawan had set up a potentially successful run chase.

The Hammersmith and City Line and part of the Circle Line have been suspended due to a fire at a 24-storey building in London, with Transport for London closing the lines at the request of the London Fire Brigade to mitigate the risk of debris falling onto the tracks.
Jamie Hamill has signed a three-year contract with Kilmarnock, returning to the club after being previously released, and will make his second debut for the team.
During a match between Ipswich and Norwich, a fan named Ross Morgan accidentally punched a hole in his ceiling while celebrating a goal, only to be offered repairs by the goal-scorer, Paul Anderson.

In Wales, a new law requires retailers to keep cigarettes out of public view, unless customers ask for them, with shop managers and assistants facing fines of up to £5,000 and six months in prison if they fail to comply.
Bristol Rovers have signed 20-year-old Lucas, who has already made 10 appearances for the club this season, scoring three goals, and is expected to provide options in the forward areas.

Network Rail is undertaking maintenance work at Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire, including making the station watertight and rebuilding the chimney stack on the signal box, with night-time work on the platform canopy to minimize disruption.

Lawrence Phillips, a former NFL player who struggled with personal and legal issues, has been found dead, with officials believing he took his own life while serving a prison sentence of over 30 years.

The Belfast Rapid Transit (BRT) plan proposes extending bus lane operating hours from 07:30-09:30 and 15:30-18:30 to 07:00-19:00 to ensure maximum compliance and avoid confusion, with two rounds of consultation to be held.
Lionel Messi scored the winning goal in Barcelona's match against Atletico, securing his 287th La Liga goal and extending his lead as the competition's all-time top scorer.

Italian prosecutors have arrested over 70 people, including players and directors from around 30 clubs, in a match-fixing inquiry led by prosecutors in the southern town of Catanzaro, with some suspects linked to the 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate.

Around 1,600 Dolomedes plantarius spiderlings, bred as hybrids between species from Sussex and Suffolk, have been released into a dyke at Castle Marshes to help establish a new population with increased genetic diversity.
The Partition of India in 2017 marked the independence of two new countries, resulting in millions of people becoming refugees as they were no longer under British rule.

Iva Barr, a seasoned marathon runner who participated in the first London Marathon in 1981, completed about 14 miles of the route before finishing her 20th marathon by walking the final part to the finish line.

In China's top cities, the extremely high demand for property has led some couples to undergo fake divorces in order to buy additional homes, despite efforts by the central bank to control rising prices.
A 46-year-old landlord, Mr Jones, died at a public house in Holyhead, and a 24-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murder following a stand-off with police.
This text does not appear to be an article, but rather a series of promotional statements and contact information for the BBC News Entertainment team.

Two men, Antony Sztuka and Scott Kennedy, died in a car crash near Carsphairn, Scotland, when a red Ford Fiesta collided with a white Asda delivery van, and police are seeking information from witnesses who may have seen a white flat-bed pickup truck involved in the incident.

Australian rower Sarah Tait, who won an Olympic silver medal in the women's pair in 2012, was an inspiration to many young athletes and a role model for emerging female athletes, despite her untimely passing after being diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2013.
In the aftermath of a deal allowing US troops to stay in Afghanistan after 2014, the Taliban claimed responsibility for two bombings in Kabul that injured several people and killed at least 15.

Daimler, the parent company of Mercedes-Benz, reported a 6% increase in sales of cars and commercial vehicles in the second quarter, with a predicted full-year sales total of "significantly more than 100bn euros".

A 10-year-old son of Crown Prince Frederik of Denmark was rescued by a lifeguard, Nick Malcolm, at Mermaid Beach on the Gold Coast after being caught in a rip current, with officials initially downplaying the incident.
A fire in Elgin Road, Scotland, resulted in the discovery of an elderly man's body, with police indicating that initial investigations suggest no suspicious circumstances.

Veterans with amputation-related medical issues can now access specialized treatment at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre (DMRC) at Headley Court, near Epsom, following a new clinic setup that aims to provide the best possible care for those who have made significant sacrifices for Britain's safety.

Since the enforcement cameras in Port Talbot went live, around 125 drivers per day have been caught exceeding the speed limit, a reduction from the 700 drivers per day caught during a pilot period before Christmas.

A Manchester-born teacher, arrested in Spain as part of an Interpol investigation, is suspected of secretly taking photographs of his students and sharing images of minors with others online, with police discovering a large number of sexually explicit files involving minors at his home.

A sturgeon named Steve, who escaped from a Hampshire aquarium due to flooding in February, has been found a mile away at a local car wash, and is reported to be only "a little worse for wear" after his ordeal.
Chris Rock, a comedian and actor, has filed for divorce from his wife of 19 years, Malaak Compton-Rock, and is requesting privacy as they navigate the divorce process.
A multi-vehicle collision on the motorway at Tamnamore, between junctions 13 and 14, has caused the road to be closed in both directions, resulting in significant traffic disruptions.

The French government has nominated senior diplomat Laurent Stefanini as its new ambassador to the Vatican, but the Vatican has yet to respond, sparking speculation that the nomination may be rejected due to the long silence, which is typically a sign of a declined appointment.
The Nasdaq composite index fell 2.4% to close at 4,876, its biggest one-day drop since April 10 last year, despite Kraft Foods' shares surging over 35% after a merger announcement.

Marketa Vondrousova, a Czech tennis player ranked 233rd in the world, won her first ATP title at the Grand Prix Hassan II, while Borna Coric of Croatia secured his first ATP title by defeating Philipp Kohlschreiber of Germany.
Stoke City has signed Eric Choupo-Moting, a 28-year-old former Germany youth international, as their fourth summer signing ahead of the Premier League season opener against Everton.

A 56-year-old man, Seamus McCollum, who had cerebral palsy and lived at a private nursing home in Maine, Randalstown, was treated as a murder victim only after an autopsy in April, nearly six months after his death in September.

Heavy rains triggered by a depression in the Bay of Bengal have caused widespread flooding and disruptions in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, with thousands evacuated and a relief fund of 5 billion rupees announced.

A McGill's bus caught fire on the A760 Kilbirnie Road near Largs on Saturday, but thanks to the driver's quick actions, all passengers, including a partially-sighted woman's mother, were safely evacuated with no injuries reported.

Jake Ball, a 25-year-old English cricketer, has made a strong start to the 2016 County Championship season, taking six wickets in each of Notts' first two games and being praised by his team for his impressive form with the new ball.

A memorial stone, made from Jersey granite, has been unveiled in the French village of Guillemont to commemorate the 120 Jersey men who died during the Battle of the Somme, with a core of the stone being brought back to Jersey to form part of a monument in Royal Square.
John Boyega, a 24-year-old actor who played stormtrooper Finn in Star Wars: The Force Awakens, has returned to his childhood theatre company, Theatre Peckham, to give back to his roots.
England's Luke Donald shot a 65 to move into contention, four strokes behind the leaders, Aphibarnrat and Fitzpatrick, at the European Tour event.

Middlesex ended day one of their County Championship match against Hampshire with a strong position, Voges remaining unbeaten on 128 and the hosts finishing at 342-3, despite losing two early wickets.
A 52-year-old woman has died and a 16-year-old boy is critically injured in an incident on Penilee Road, with police having now located a 54-year-old man they were seeking to speak to.

A three-bedroom house at 9 Newcastle Road, Wavertree, where John Lennon, a member of The Beatles, lived as a child, has been sold to an anonymous telephone bidder after a bidding war at a price likely to be between £150,000 and £250,000.

A 29-year-old man, Aaron Joseph, has been charged with owning a dog that was dangerously out of control, after a 52-year-old man, David Ellam, was fatally injured while walking his Yorkshire terrier near Huddersfield last August.

A body has been found on private land near Leighton, about 10 miles from the centre of Shrewsbury, which is believed to be that of 22-year-old Thomas Bebbington who was last seen entering a river on November 10.
Five-week-old baby otters are doing well and require six feeds a day, with plans to eventually move them to an outdoor enclosure with a pool and feed them live food by the summer.
Police in Newtownards are seeking witnesses to a bonfire disturbance on Monday and any activity around a home, where a 33-year-old mother-of-four, Joanne Thompson, was found deceased on Wednesday.
A record number of 2,270 black-tailed godwits spent time on the Scottish island of Tiree this spring, with many stopping to refuel before migrating to Iceland.
Giovanni Durrant, a long-serving coach and former player at Rangers, will not return to the club after being left without a position by manager Mark Warburton.
A rare albino deer has gained attention from visitors due to its unusual occurrence, estimated to happen once every 100,000 births.

A 13-year-old boy, Asad Khan, died three weeks after starting at Beckfoot Upper Heaton School in Bradford, with his family claiming he was bullied, and an inquest is ongoing to investigate the circumstances surrounding his death.

A mysterious painting depicting a 1654 ceremony has been restored and is being researched by experts, who are unsure of its origin, painter, or value, after being found to have hung in Rokeby Park since at least 1880.
Macclesfield Town secured a 3-0 win over Wrexham, with goals from Danny Rowe, Mitch Hancox, and Danny Whittaker, lifting them to seventh in the table.

French oil and gas company Total has partnered with the Confederation of African Football (Caf) as the new headline sponsor for 10 competitions, including the 2017 Africa Cup of Nations finals in Gabon.

Spain's coach, Lopetegui, has announced a new squad for World Cup qualifiers, recalling players like Diego Costa and Juan Mata, while omitting Iker Casillas from the lineup for matches against Belgium and Liechtenstein.
A large wildfire, believed to have been started deliberately, has spread across a 5-kilometre area, crossing the border, with 45 firefighters, including Irish crew members, working to contain it.

Former English cricketer Boyd Rankin has made a timely comeback to Ireland, becoming eligible to play again after a two-year absence, and is set to feature in the upcoming ICC World Twenty20 in India.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, established with the Patient Client Council, aims to provide an independent voice and improve treatment and care for individuals and families affected by rare diseases in Northern Ireland.

Gloucester Cathedral plans to introduce girl choristers to its choir, which was established by Henry VIII in 1539, in an effort to discover talented young girls from diverse backgrounds and backgrounds to join the cathedral's musical worship.
Pedro, a 29-year-old Chelsea winger, suffered a concussion in a recent game in Beijing, but is expected to be okay and will wear a protective mask upon returning to training.
Nottinghamshire has appointed James Taylor as a batting coach and former Northants captain David Sales to work with the county's batsmen, bringing their extensive cricket experience to the team.
A man has been charged with multiple offenses, including assault on police, after an incident on the Whiterock Road in Belfast on Friday afternoon.
A volunteer crew from the Larne RNLI launched two lifeboats to assist a yacht whose engine had failed off the coast, successfully towing it to Carrick Marina.
Ipswich Town secured a 3-2 win over MK Dons, with goals from David McGoldrick, Brett Pitman, and a header from Varney, despite MK Dons' Revell scoring twice from the spot and a free-kick.

A man from Darlington has been issued a summons to appear in court on charges of dangerous driving and other offenses after a motorway bridge collapsed onto a London-bound carriageway, injuring a motorcyclist.

A group of around 200 people, organized by several Germans, staged a flashmob in the Costa Brava town of Platja d'Aro, pretending to chase a celebrity, which caused widespread panic and led to 11 people being treated for injuries.

Two people, Sindyann Regis and Chevaze Mcgregor, have been charged with murder after a two-and-a-half-year-old boy, Jeremiah Regis, was found with over 100 injuries, including a bite to the chest, and later died from abdominal peritonitis caused by blunt force trauma.

A large gorse fire on Woodbury Common in Devon has engulfed a significant area, with firefighters battling the flames amid challenging conditions including high winds and limited water supplies, and nearby residents have been evacuated as a precaution.
The British Speedway Promoters' Association has announced that an agreement has been reached to keep Leicester Speedway club going, with a 15-year lease also signed for the team's venue.

A 50-year-old woman, Elizabeth Bowe, was found badly injured in St Andrews and died three days later, with her 51-year-old brother, Charles Gordon, being charged with her murder and remanded in custody.

Ross County has signed 29-year-old midfielder Jim O'Brien on a two-year contract after his successful loan stint last season, with manager Jim McIntyre expressing enthusiasm for the player's experience and potential to develop younger squad members.

Northants' seam attack restricted Durham to 59-3 in a 45.2-over innings, with Buck and McCarthy taking key wickets, before the visitors suffered a setback in their own reply due to the loss of several batsmen.

New Zealand's Ko is one shot behind joint leaders Brooke Henderson and Lee Mi-rim at the halfway stage of the second women's major of the year, after a tough round at the Sahalee Country Club in Seattle.
Gordon Watson has rejoined the Scotland national team as assistant to manager Gordon Strachan, alongside Mark McGhee, in a role he previously held during the Euro 2008 qualifying campaign.
The Belfast Giants secured a 5-3 win over the Cardiff Devils, with a strong second period performance that saw them take control of the game and ultimately seal the victory.

At the 2016 Masters, Jordan Spieth experienced a sudden collapse, carding a quadruple-bogey seven on the 12th hole, which led to Danny Willett becoming the first Englishman to win the tournament since 1996.

The BBC invites viewers to share their photos of England for consideration in "England's Big Picture" by emailing, posting on social media, or tweeting, with contributors retaining copyright but granting a non-exclusive license for the BBC to use their images.

A 35-year-old eye specialist, Honey Rose, is on trial for gross negligence manslaughter after allegedly failing to detect a life-threatening condition during a routine eye test, which led to the death of a patient, Vincent Barker, five months later in 2012.
China's food price inflation rose to 4.9% in June, a figure above expectations but still below the government's 3.5% target, which may reduce the likelihood of interest rate cuts.
Ivory Coast international footballer Cheick Tiote, who played for Newcastle in the UK, has died after collapsing during training with Chinese second-tier side Beijing Enterprises on June 5.
Slovak rider Peter Sagan won the 5th stage of the race, with Nairo Quintana maintaining his lead overall, while Geraint Thomas rose to 6th place.

Cuadrilla's plans for fracking at its Preston New Road site in Lancashire have been approved, with the company pledging to prioritize job creation, investment, and community initiatives in the county despite ongoing legal challenges.

Three teenage males from north-west London, who were feared to be traveling to Syria, were arrested and later released without charge after being detained at Istanbul's airport upon their return to the UK.

A respiratory consultant at the Royal Berkshire Hospital, Dr Christopher Davies, questioned the high price of £22.95 for a blackout blind purchased from Homebase, suggesting that the hospital's quote rejection highlights issues with how NHS funds are used.
The Swansea City development squad won the cup final and secured 31 wins across all competitions in the 2016-17 season, following the senior team's survival in the Premier League.

Denbighshire councillors are considering creating a secondary dune system at Barkby Beach in Prestatyn to strengthen the defences against potential flooding, following severe storms in 2013 that damaged the existing dune system.
South Shields, who appeared at Wembley last season, will host Bridlington Town in a live-streamed match on August 19, with commentary provided by Conor McNamara and Danny Webber.

Police in Scotland are investigating a targeted attack on a property, in which a 38-year-old man suffered serious facial injuries and a 49-year-old man was unharmed, and are urging witnesses to come forward with information.

Pamela McLaggan pleaded guilty to manslaughter after Jonathan Baines was found dead at a house in Gainsborough, with the court hearing that Baines had been out at a race meeting before visiting pubs in the town.

A 15-year-old boy was attacked by a man and woman in their 40s at Patterton station on October 3, suffering facial injuries, and his mobile phone was stolen, with police seeking witnesses who were on a train arriving at Neilston shortly before the incident.

Two 17-year-old boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, from Dewsbury, are feared to have traveled to Syria to join the Islamic State in March, prompting an investigation by West Yorkshire Police and counter-terrorism officers.

The Great Britain ice hockey team has announced a 22-man squad for the 2016 Olympic Qualifiers, featuring several familiar faces from their 2015 World Championship team, ahead of their matches against Italy, Netherlands, and Serbia in February.
A tribute to James Burrows, the creator of the popular sitcom "Friends," is set to air on NBC on February 21, with the show's former stars, including Matthew Perry, expected to participate.

Jones, a 31-year-old footballer, has played for various clubs including Manchester United, and has made 41 league appearances for Burnley in the previous season, helping them win the Championship title.

A lawyer, Joe Acquaro, was found shot dead outside a Melbourne cafe he owned, with investigators suspecting that underworld figures may have put a price on his head due to his representation of crime bosses.

Air France flight AF374 from Paris to Vancouver was diverted to Glasgow Prestwick after a slight smell of burning was detected on board, and passengers were later flown back to Charles de Gaulle Airport on a second aircraft.

A severe weather warning has been issued for Britain as the remains of Hurricane Gonzalo are expected to bring strong winds and heavy rain, particularly affecting coastal areas and north-western Wales on Tuesday.
People are concerned about overcrowding in hospitals, which may lead to long wait times for patients, including children who need medical attention.

A 64-year-old man, Kenneth David Dickie, has died from a head injury sustained in Poole, and two individuals, a 34-year-old man and a 57-year-old woman, have been charged and bailed in connection with his death.
Nottingham Forest has extended the stay of 24-year-old forward Matteo Macheda until the end of the season, while also signing midfielder David Vaughan to a one-year contract.

The body of Christopher Huxtable, a 34-year-old man from Swansea who had been missing since a building collapse in February, was finally found and returned to his family, bringing them closure, while two other men, Ken Cresswell and John Shaw, remain missing.

Bristol City head coach Lee Johnson is optimistic ahead of a crucial match against QPR, despite the uncertainty of his team's fitness, and believes a win could significantly impact the league standings.

Luca, an ESA astronaut, described his spacewalking experience as "absolutely fantastic" after participating in two spacewalks and traveling over 110 million km during his mission to the International Space Station in 2013.
Joe Arundel, a former England Knights player, has joined Hull FC, a new club for him, expressing excitement and nervousness about the challenge ahead.

Ulster Bank, a subsidiary of RBS, has identified and fixed a problem affecting approximately 600,000 payments, with customers advised to visit a branch or contact call centres to ensure they are not left out of pocket.
Tanzania secured a 2-1 victory over Kenya in a match, while Ethiopia defeated Uganda 4-1 in a separate play-off for third place.
McDonald's Japan is rationing French fries due to a shortage caused by industrial action in the US, where dockworkers are on strike, affecting potato imports.

The 2024 Epsom Derby is shaping up with the addition of new entrants, including the favourite Cracksman, and a long-shot filly Diore Lia, who will be ridden by apprentice Gina Mangan, despite her low odds of 1,000-1.
Antoine Griezmann, Atletico Madrid's top scorer with six La Liga goals, will miss France's friendly against Ivory Coast due to a haematoma on his left foot, but an X-ray showed no bone injury.

Veteran rugby league player Willie Mason, who played 290 NRL games and won a Premiership with Canterbury in 2004, has joined the Super League's Dragons, bringing his physical and aggressive playing style to the team.
A recent survey by The Marine Conservation Society found an 11% increase in dog mess on UK beaches, with a 71% rise in Scotland, but also reported a decrease in overall litter levels.

The Supreme Court ruled that the government's introduction of fees for employment tribunal cases in 2013 was unlawful and indirectly discriminatory to women, as it disproportionately affected those bringing discrimination cases.
Wycombe secured a 2-1 win over Dagenham & Redbridge, with Paris Cowan-Hall's headed goal proving decisive, despite the hosts playing with ten men for most of the match.
Bee-eaters, native to southern Europe, have successfully bred at Low Gelt Quarry in the UK for a second consecutive summer, with chicks expected to fledge in the next few weeks.

A boy jumped into the River Wey in Guildford to try and save his father after his boat capsized, but the boy was warned by members of the public to return to safety, while a search operation is underway to locate the missing kayaker.

A young girl visiting Rabat Zoo in Morocco was struck and killed by a stone thrown by an elephant that had managed to get past its enclosure, with the zoo stating that such incidents are rare and unpredictable.

New Labour MP, Ms Glass, has been appointed to the shadow cabinet as education minister, but her appointment comes amidst a wave of resignations and calls for a leadership election, with her predecessor, Ms Powell, citing that Jeremy Corbyn's position as party leader has become "untenable".
Chelsea manager Conte believes that six teams, including Chelsea, Manchester United, and others, are strong contenders to win the title with 14 games remaining.

A dispersal order has been issued in Llangefni, allowing police and community support officers to force young troublemakers to leave the area and potentially ban them from the area for up to 24 hours.

Boro manager Garry Monk has expressed interest in signing Chelsea midfielder Lewis Baker, while also confirming the team's recent signing of De Roon, who has played 33 Premier League games for the club.
The Roald Dahl Funny Prize, established in 2008 to honor humorous children's books, is set to be relaunched in 2016 as part of Roald Dahl's centenary celebrations.

Frazier Glenn Miller Jr., a 74-year-old white supremacist, was sentenced to death for the murders of three people outside Jewish sites in Kansas, and in response, he shouted "heil Hitler" before being removed from the courtroom.

A city council plans to launch a self-service bike scheme in April 2017, with 500 bikes located across the city, and aims to secure a provider to supply and operate the scheme at no cost to taxpayers.

Sakho, a 27-year-old Senegal international, has returned to light training after back surgery and is now in a period similar to his pre-season training schedule, requiring time to build up his strength and fitness before being considered for Premier League selection.

According to the NI Residential Property Price Index, property prices in Northern Ireland rose by 5.4% annually compared to 2015, but remained relatively flat at 0.8% compared to the second quarter of the same year.

A recent delivery of a giant wind turbine part on the A713 in Dumfries and Galloway ended in an accident, with the lorry and its cargo ending up in a ditch, highlighting the challenges of transporting large loads on country roads.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board is considering downgrading services at some district hospitals due to staffing shortages, but is facing opposition from residents who worry about the impact on maternity care and travel distances.

South Africa's Mignon du Preez hit a second ODI century, scoring 116 off 99 balls, to help her side to a 272-6 total, which they eventually won by 68 runs against Ireland, who were bowled out for 204.
Peake, a 30-year-old athlete, aims to break her own Welsh record at the Cardiff International Sports Stadium and qualify for Team GB in Rio by surpassing the 4.50m qualification standard.
A fire at a building site in Llanwern, Wales, burned for over 10 hours before being extinguished, and police are investigating the blaze which is believed to have been deliberately set.

A charity event, organized by Mercy Corps with the help of the Nepal Scotland Association and the city council, was held in Edinburgh to raise money for the relief efforts following the devastating earthquake in Nepal.
Uefa has imposed a suspension on Hibernian head coach Neil Lennon for "acts of violence against the referee" during a Europa League qualifying match, and the club is currently appealing the decision.
A fire broke out at the ICL UK Boulby mine, located 1,100m under the sea bed, on April 13, injuring seven workers and prompting an investigation by the Health and Safety Executive.

Two men, including a 23-year-old British national, Adam Burton, were removed from the Machu Picchu Unesco World Heritage site in Peru after being caught posing naked, but have not been arrested or charged.
Croatian international Ivan Rakitic is set to sign a new deal with Barcelona, reportedly worth £109m with a buyout clause, on Friday.
A couple from Halstead suffered "life-changing" injuries during a two-hour home invasion on April 26, with the woman remaining in a critical condition and the man still receiving treatment.

The Wickerman Festival, taking place on July 25-26, has announced its lineup, including a headline performance by Dizzee Rascal on the opening night, alongside other acts such as Martha Reeves and The Vandellas and Big Country.

Northampton Saints' Tom Foden expressed hope that his team's strong performance will help England rugby, with the possibility of several Saints players being selected for the upcoming Six Nations tournament.
A 22-year-old motorcyclist died after a collision between a KTM motorcycle and a Vauxhall Zafira car in Dagenham, with a 10-year-old boy from the car remaining in a serious condition.

Pfizer has agreed to acquire California-based Anacor Pharmaceuticals, the developer of eczema cream crisaborole, which is awaiting US FDA approval and could reach $2 billion in annual sales if approved.
Police responded to a street fight in Dagenham, arresting two teenage boys, and recovered several knives, scissors, and cannabis from the scene, with no reported injuries.
A 23-year-old man from Cardiff was arrested on suspicion of sexual assault after a 19-year-old woman reported being attacked near Cardiff Civic Centre.

A by-election is to be held in the Scottish constituency of Berwickshire, Roxburgh and Selkirk, where Conservative candidate John Lamont is seeking to unseat SNP MP Calum Kerr, with the election to take place within five weeks.

The European Union has gained access to new markets for its beef exports, including Canada, after the country agreed to recognize the EU's robust measures to eradicate Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).

European finance ministers have agreed to create a single EU list of "non-cooperative jurisdictions" by the end of the summer, in response to the Panama Papers leak and to crack down on tax havens and money laundering.

During the construction of the West Link road in Inverness, archaeologists discovered Bronze Age burnt mounds, pottery fragments, and kiln remains, which suggest ancient practices of heating stones for potential use in cooking, washing, or as small saunas.
Main scored for the Latics after the hour mark, securing a victory that leaves Oldham with a comfortable cushion above the League One relegation places.
The article reports the peaceful passing of Irish actor Lally, who had a successful career in both Irish and international productions, including soap operas, films, and television series.
Derby City Council has decided to keep Moorways Pool open for at least a year after initially planning to close it to save £350,000 annually, following a petition signed by over 4,000 people.

The UN has expressed concerns about the detention of children in a military barracks in Maiduguri, north-eastern Nigeria, who were previously living in areas controlled by Boko Haram, with no clear details on their ages or the length of their detention.
Hearts head coach Robbie Neilson is considering signing experienced goalkeeper Lee Hollis, who became a free agent after leaving Motherwell this summer.

Chelsey Lee, a 26-year-old American basketball player who played in the Women's Korean Basketball League, is suspected of fabricating her Korean ancestry to qualify for the league's foreign player quota, leading to a potential lifetime suspension and annulment of her records.

A new app released by UK regulator Ofcom helps users identify and troubleshoot potential issues slowing down their Wi-Fi speeds, which research suggests are not as fast as they could be in six million homes and offices.

Manchester United players Paul Pogba and Zlatan Ibrahimovic discussed the role of social media and pressure in the game, with Ibrahimovic stating that top players are not affected by external pressure but instead put pressure on themselves to perform.

A metal object, later confirmed to be a payload shroud from the Alphasat satellite launched by the UK Space Agency in July, was found floating in a river in Brazil's northern Para state, and authorities have asked the UK Space Agency to collect it.

Former Labour culture minister James Purnell warned that decriminalizing non-payment of the TV licence fee could lead to increased non-payment and cost the BBC £200m, forcing either the closure of popular channels or a higher licence fee.
Harps earned their first win over Derry since 1998, coming from behind to secure a 2-1 victory with goals from David Scully and Ryan Curran, despite Rory Patterson's late consolation goal for Derry.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has stated that issuers of "distributed ledger or blockchain technology-based securities" must register their offers and sales, in an effort to protect investors and maintain market integrity amid concerns over the rise of Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs).

Operation Anagram, a Strathclyde Police investigation formed in 2006 to track serial killer Peter Tobin, has brought closure to some families of his victims, including Vicky Hamilton and Dinah McNicol, and will continue to investigate new information that may lead to further convictions.

At the Australian Grand Prix, Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel edged out Mercedes' Lewis Hamilton, but both drivers remain optimistic about their chances in the season, with Hamilton looking to turn the tables at the Chinese race.

A man, who was a high-profile lawyer representing several notable celebrities during his career, is on trial at Southwark Crown Court for allegedly committing indecent assault in his London office in the 1980s, with the prosecution having finished its case and the trial adjourned until Monday.
